questions.question: When you make an emergency stop on the roadside, do you need to use your parking brake?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Always set your parking brake during an emergency roadside stop. Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow X on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to change to a red X.
The signal is about to change to a green arrow.
Drivers may drive normally in this lane.
Drivers may drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The signal is about to change to a red X.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow X means you should leave the lane. A red X will appear next. Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed and tell you when toll booths are operating.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going. Always be careful around motorcyclists.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver holds their left arm down, they are signaling that they will stop. Change your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: What do round signs warn you about?

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Railroad crossings ahead.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings ahead.
questions.explanation: Round signs warn you that a railroad crossing is coming. Drive carefully when you see this sign.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians cross first.
Go faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: You can turn right or left at a steady green light unless a sign says you cannot. You must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection cross before you turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.
No passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is starting ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roads with a center divider. Stay in your right lane.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Move into the lane the arrow points to.
Slow down and stop if you can.
Turn left after checking for traffic and pedestrians.
Go because you have the right of way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if you can.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You need to back out of your driveway and see children nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk behind your car to make sure it is clear.
Tell the children to leave the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk behind your car to make sure it is clear.
questions.explanation: Always look through your back window and mirrors when backing up. Do not trust mirrors alone, especially when children are near. Get out and check behind your car before you back up or out of your driveway.

questions.question: Your vehicle starts to skid. What should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel sharply the other way.
Turn your steering wheel toward traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer in the same direction the car is sliding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that the road ahead has low clearance.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed. Solid lines cannot be crossed. You may cross a solid yellow line only when you are turning.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren, but you cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not headed toward you.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb:

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. This stops your vehicle from rolling into traffic. On streets without a curb, turn your wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause excessive oil use.
Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than normal.
Make you drowsy while driving.
Set grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases from the engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust system can make you drowsy while driving. These fumes can be dangerous and cause serious harm.

questions.question: Regulatory signs:

options.text: Are placed in every location where there is a present danger.
Indicate what a driver must or must not do.
Are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
May warn drivers that they are approaching a school zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Indicate what a driver must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular and white with black markings. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. These signs show speed limits, prohibit passing or turning, and clarify other driving rules.

questions.question: When driving in fog:

options.text: Use your parking lights.
Use your low beams.
Use your high beams.
It makes no difference which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle downhill on a two-way street:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road. If your vehicle rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: You may not park within ____ of a fire hydrant.

options.text: 40 feet
20 feet
10 feet
Five feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 feet
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant. Park in a location where other drivers can see your vehicle from both directions.

questions.question: What do diamond symbols on pavement markings and signs mean?

options.text: School zones.
Carpool lanes.
Construction areas.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carpool lanes.
questions.explanation: Diamond symbols mark carpool lanes. These lanes are for vehicles with two or more occupants. They are usually on the far left side of a freeway and separated by white or yellow lines.

questions.question: When should you slow down when exiting a highway?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first. Then slow down. Do not slow down before you enter the exit lane.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect your vehicle's stopping distance?

options.text: Your own reaction time.
The time of day.
The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
The condition and type of your vehicle's tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road condition, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but driving faster is illegal. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, and bad weather, even if no sign tells you to.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You may never stop your vehicle there.
You may park there if the driver remains in the vehicle.
You may stop temporarily only to pickup or discharge passengers.
You may stop to load or unload merchandise.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may stop temporarily only to pickup or discharge passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign allows only a temporary stop to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Is never used as a traffic signal.
Has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light.
Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.
Means that the traffic the arrow is pointing toward must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a circular red light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What should you do first when visibility decreases?

options.text: Turning on your headlights.
Reducing your speed.
Turning on your windshield wipers.
Looking for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your speed.
questions.explanation: Your first response to poor visibility and dangerous conditions is to slow down.

questions.question: When can you drive above the posted speed limit?

options.text: Never.
When legally passing another vehicle on a highway with a speed limit of 55 mph or above.
When there is no police officer present.
When you are in a hurry.

questions.correctAnswerText: When legally passing another vehicle on a highway with a speed limit of 55 mph or above.
questions.explanation: Driving faster than the speed limit is illegal. However, on highways with a speed limit of 55 mph or higher, you may go 10 mph faster when legally passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What does a red flashing traffic light mean?

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder.
No parking at any time.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane to avoid a hazard ahead.
